scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the user is in the right for feeling frustrated with his girlfriend about her bragging about her job perks. Let me break this down step by step. First, the girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours, just needs to work 35 hours a week whenever it's convenient. She can work from home sometimes, has full benefits despite not being full-time, a nice retirement package, and the company pays for continued education. She works in cutting-edge robotics, gets along with her coworkers, has a lot of PTO, and her boss even lets them earn more PTO by working extra hours. Her team's managers buy them expensive office stuff like a $500 espresso maker and fancy furniture. They're paid well too, with a mid-level salary in robotics, which is still good. She prefers more time over being a top earner. Initially, the user thought it was great that she found something she's happy with. But recently, it's become frustrating because she seems to forget that not everyone has such a job. When they're out with friends or just hanging out, she talks about the nice stuff her managers bought, all the vacations she takes, how she and her coworkers left the office mid-day to see a movie and came back later. It seems like she doesn't realize this isn't normal. Last night at a party, she mentioned touring apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and someone asked if she had work. She said, "Yeah, but I can set my own hours." That rubbed the user the wrong way, and he told her to stop going on about her work perks, calling it obnoxious and braggy. She defended herself, saying she was just explaining something, and he said it wasn't just this one thing, but everything. He pointed out that most people don't live the life she does. She accused him of being jealous and said he should look at what he's feeling jealous of and what he needs to do to get it. He told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest. She said he's the only one with a problem and stormed off. The user is asking if he's AITA (Are You The Asshole) for what he said. So, to determine if he's in the right, I need to consider both perspectives. On one hand, the girlfriend has a great job with many perks, and she's proud of her achievements. She worked hard to get there, and it's natural to want to share that with others. However, the user feels that she's bragging and forgets that not everyone has such a job. He's frustrated because her constant talking about her perks makes him feel like she's not considering others' situations. I think it's important to balance pride in one's job with sensitivity to others' feelings. While it's okay to be proud, constantly bringing up job perks in social settings can come off as bragging, especially if others don't have similar opportunities. The user's frustration seems valid because it's affecting their social interactions and relationship. On the other hand, the girlfriend feels that she earned her job through hard work and doesn't see why she shouldn't talk about it. She might not realize how her comments are affecting the user. It's possible that she doesn't intend to brag but is just sharing her experiences. In this situation, communication is key. The user expressed his feelings, but the girlfriend took it as jealousy. Maybe the user could have approached the conversation differently, focusing on how her comments make him feel rather than accusing her of bragging. However, the user did express his feelings, which is a positive step. Considering all this, I think the user is not entirely in the wrong. It's reasonable to feel frustrated when a partner's behavior affects the relationship negatively. However, he could have communicated his feelings more gently to avoid making the girlfriend feel attacked. The girlfriend, in turn, should be more mindful of how her comments affect others, especially in social settings. So, in conclusion, while the user's feelings are valid, he could have handled the situation more sensitively. Therefore, he's not entirely AITA, but there's room for improvement in how he communicates his concerns.
